lesson_title: Cut One Link: How Every Contraceptive Really Works
hook_text: Out of 100 couples using nothing for a year, about 85 get pregnant. Here is the honest scoreboard.
clip_script: Pregnancy is a chain: an egg released, a sperm meeting it, a ball of cells moving into the uterus. Every contraceptive cuts one link. The pill, the injection and the implant stop the egg being released. The condom stops the sperm reaching the egg. The copper loop stops the move-in. Now the honest scoreboard, 100 couples, one year, real life. Nothing: about 85 pregnancies. Pulling out: about 20. Condoms: about 13. The pill: about 7, because people forget. The injection: about 4. The implant or the loop: less than 1, because you cannot forget them. But here is the twist. Which of those also stops HIV and other infections? Only one. The condom. The pill does nothing against germs. That is why clinics say: dual protection. A condom every time, plus a reliable method. And from age 12, any clinic must keep your visit private. Not having sex at all? Zero pregnancies, zero infections. Know the scoreboard. Choose for yourself.
visual_style: A three-link chain with scissors cutting each link in turn; a scoreboard counts down from 85 to under 1 with method icons; a shield appears over the condom only.
pacing: Brisk chain beats, a countdown rhythm on the scoreboard, a pause before the twist, a calm finish.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and explain why dual protection beats any single method.
